parsed.explanation: The traveller-facing regime is mostly benign: no expression criminalisation, self-ID since 2016, pride protected and officially attended, constitutional gender-identity protection, conversion ban. No documented border, document, or facility friction for visitors. The dominant exposure is custody: birth-sex male placement is documented operating on visitors (a foreign national in 2023 denied protective housing and medical care), with a recurring, unremedied pattern of sexual violence, beatings, deaths (2021, 2026) and no functioning remedy. That is tier-1/tier-2 severity on the detention path, offsetting strong ordinary-stay safety. Rising LGBTQ violence amid armed conflict lacks quantification; 2011 police-investigation failures are dated. Post-2026 legislative backsliding (118-0 adoption ban) is a climate signal. Net: safe daily travel, severe custody if detained; lands just above the 0.55 band, at the low edge of Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border, visa or document-mismatch friction for trans visitors appears in the dossier.
entry_documents.protection: Self-ID law (2016, streamlined 2024) and constitutional gender-identity protection signal document-respecting institutions; no documented visitor refusals either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport marker governs at entry; no documented checks or secondary screening reported.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented, severe, recurring: trans women placed in male pavilions in an almost universally male prison system; sexual violence, torture, forced head-shaving, beatings targeting implants; deaths in custody (2021 massacre, 2026); a foreign-national trans woman in 2023 denied protective placement and HIV care. Remedy petitions and oversight calls have not changed practice across 2011–2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Protective 'prioritaria' pavilion exists but documented as used unevenly; 2016 protocol-development decision not shown implemented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visitor detention (even unrelated) routes into birth-sex placement; no documented consular or judicial override of placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for visitor-facing facilities (bathrooms, hotels, transport). Custody placement is the facilities exposure, covered above.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitutional anti-discrimination covers gender identity; no facility bans documented.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; prison health-care barriers documented for trans detainees (no exams, withheld HIV treatment in male pavilion).
care_services.protection: Conversion practices criminalised (Art. 151, torture-equivalent) — protective in principle; hundreds of clinics still promoting as of 2023, enforcement not documented.
care_services.interaction: If detained, care access becomes the documented exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2011 report: police and prosecutors not thoroughly investigating LGBT deaths; macho, negative social climate. Dated; no current police-targeting pattern documented. Rising anti-LGBTQ violence (2024) amid armed conflict, unquantified.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Office-holder hostility penalised (2013 candidate fined); pride marches authorised with police protection and official participation since 1998.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police protection at public events documented; investigation quality uncertain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented as traveller-facing. Adolescent legal-recognition status unresolved (2024-25 rulings vs. March 2026 overview saying under-18s excluded). Education-access violations and clinic confinement findings are 2011 and resident-facing.
minors_guardians.protection: Court-ordered registration of same-sex couple's child (2018).
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's document status uncertain but visitor documents are home-issued; no documented border consequence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Monitoring group documented 27 LGBTQ+ murders in 2023 with inadequate official response; violence rising amid armed conflict; no denominator or trans-specific rate, so magnitude unclear.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Large, protected pride events; constitutional recourse exists on paper.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Investigation failures documented only from 2011; current police response not established.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Custody remedy shown not to work: repeated complaints, oversight calls and an uninvestigated 2026 death over 15 years. Post-2011 official monitoring not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working courts shown for residents (registry orders, adolescent rulings); no visitor-facing remedy case documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule-of-law machinery exists but is unproven for trans detainees; no documented working visitor remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both feature birth-sex male prison placement with assault risk and protective housing used unevenly. But 0.25-C adds a cross-dressing statute enabling routine arrests of visitors; this jurisdiction criminalises nothing about expression, has self-ID, protected pride, and no documented visitor arrests — materially safer than the 0.25 anchor.

0.55-C's worst exposure is ward assignment and delayed care — friction without lethal outcomes. This jurisdiction's custody axis is worse: documented sexual violence, torture allegations and two deaths, including a foreign national, recurring without remedy. But its everyday axes (documents, facilities, police) are cleaner than 0.55-C's. Mixed, slightly better than 0.55 overall.

0.75-C has humiliating but brief border detention with functioning appeal, compensation and counsel. This jurisdiction's ordinary travel is comparable or better, but its custody path has no working remedy and lethal documented outcomes — a materially worse worst case. Sits below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime offers strong climate-level protection — constitutional coverage, self-ID, decriminalisation, conversion ban, officially protected pride — and documents no border, document or facility friction for trans visitors, so an adult or adult-with-minor traveller who avoids detention faces mostly friction-level risk. The exposure that pulls the score down is the detention pathway: birth-sex placement in a nearly all-male prison system, documented since 2011 through 2026 with sexual violence, beatings, withheld medical care, and two deaths, including one foreign-national trans woman denied the protective pavilion in 2023. Oversight findings recur without changing practice, so the custody exposure is corroborated, not mitigated. Unquantified rising violence amid armed conflict and a conservative social climate, plus a 2026 legislative backsliding signal, keep the score from the upper 0.7s; the clean everyday regime keeps it well clear of the 0.25-0.45 band.
